content.text: The early action inside Kaseya Center was as hot as the weather in Miami, with the athletes on the UFC 327 looking to set the tone for the evening. A series of submissions and a handful of competitive battles get the table for a clash between featherweight standouts Aaron Pico and Patricio Pitbull, who closed out the prelims in style. If you missed any of the action, get caught up by checking out the recaps below. Subscribe To Paramount+ Results, Highlights & Backstage Interviews Aaron Pico defeated Patricio Pitbull by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) Aaron Pico turned in the best performance of his career at the most opportune time, closing out Saturday’s UFC 327 prelims with a brilliant bounce-back effort against Brazilian standout Patricio Pitbull. Aaron Pico Post-Fight Interview | UFC 327 Both competitors were measured and respectful of the others’ skills in the opening frame, neither man landing anything of real great substance. But in the second, Pico started opening up, hurting Pitbull multiple times while showcasing the full range of his weaponry, carrying the momentum into the third and through the final horn. After a brutal knockout loss in his debut last summer, this was an incredible rebound performance from Pico, who should climb into the rankings when they update next week. Still just 29, he remains an intriguing figure in the featherweight division, especially if he continues to put things together like this in the future. Kevin Holland Post-Fight Interview | UFC 327 Brown appeared to be the more effective of the two in the opening stanza, cutting Holland under the right eye and landing the heavier blows during the first five minutes. Holland responded with a deep anaconda choke attempt in the second that was close, but he was forced to abandon. The third was spent largely in the clinch, both men trading short shots, leaving the verdict in the hands of the judges. When the scorecards were collected and totaled, it was Holland that came away with the win, getting himself back in the win column while earning his 16th UFC victory. Though he didn’t get the finish, this was a strong showing for the ever-active “Trail Blazer,” who will make his 30th UFC start next time out. Main Card Results | Scorecards | Watch On P+ Chris Padilla and MarQuel Mederos fight to a majority draw (28-28, 28-28, 29-27) Chris Padilla and MarQuel Mederos paired off in a terrific clash of underrated lightweights early on Saturday’s fight card, battling close for all 15 minutes. Chris Padilla and MarQuel Mederos trade punches in a lightweight fight during the UFC 327 event at Kaseya Center on April 11, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) Mederos landed the better individual blows throughout the contest, including opening Padilla up with a lead elbow in the first, but the volume and relentless pressure of Padilla was undeniable and impactful as well. Unfortunately, a second accidental eye poke late in the contest cost Mederos a point, ratcheting up the intrigue over how the scorecards would shake out. Two of the three judges scored the fight a draw, while the third had the bout in favor of Padilla, resulting in the majority draw verdict. Regardless of your thoughts on the scoring, this was an outstanding battle between a pair of unheralded talents and highlights the insane depth of talent in the lightweight ranks at the moment. Vicente Luque Post-Fight Interview | UFC 327 This was a classic Luque performance in his new weight class and not far from his home base at Kill Cliff FC. This was Luque’s third anaconda choke finish, tying him with Charles Oliveira and Makwan Amirkhani for the most in UFC history, and his 15th finish inside the Octagon overall. Main Card Results | Scorecards | Watch On P+ Charles Radtke defeated Francisco Prado by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 30-26) Charles Radtke showed the diversity of his game in the UFC 327 opener, leaning heavily on his grappling in the first two rounds before shutting down the comeback attempt of Francisco Prado to secure a lopsided decision win. Charles Radtke punches Francisco Prado in a welterweight fight during the UFC 327 event at Kaseya Center on April 11, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) Prado landed well in the opening seconds of the contest, prompted the usually aggressive gunslinger Radtke to shift gears, playing to his advantage in the grappling department over the first 10 minutes while also splitting open Prado with an elbow from the bottom. The third opened with the Argentine losing a point for a nasty eye poke, and was more of the same once it resumed, with the American Radtke controlling things on the canvas through to the final horn. Radtke claimed a clean sweep of the scorecards, with the point deduction making the margin of victory wider. That’s now consecutive wins for “Chuck Buffalo” and wins in three of last four overall, while Prado dropped his fourth straight and fifth in six UFC starts.
